title: Programming Languages
tagline: Seven decades of telling machines what to do.

events.title: FORTRAN’s debut
events.text: The first high-level programming language with a compiler, FORTRAN makes scientific computing practical.

events.title: Lisp: AI’s native tongue
events.text: John McCarthy designs Lisp, pioneering functional programming and becoming the language of early AI research.

events.title: C arrives
events.text: Dennis Ritchie creates C at Bell Labs; it becomes the lingua franca of systems programming.

events.title: Python is released
events.text: Guido van Rossum releases Python, a readable and versatile language later adopted across science and AI.

events.title: JavaScript runs the web
events.text: Brendan Eich creates JavaScript in ten days at Netscape, embedding it in every web browser.

events.title: Go is announced
events.text: Google releases Go, designed for concurrency and large-scale systems at a time of multicore CPUs.

events.title: Rust hits 1.0
events.text: Mozilla ships Rust 1.0, a memory-safe systems language that later wins hearts (and memory bugs) across industry.
